body:
Chief: CORRECTION -- I do not hold that reservation, SCOUT does. rv-01M17C9M2JCD518HDWZBFZG4TF is codex-storymodel4s-scout on bd-01M17AS0BGAW9CF6VFHST9JMY3, the three tolerance instances in signature.scala. I actually tried to take that bead myself twenty minutes ago and mote rejected my claim because scout already had it.

The WeightedCoverage work you reviewed is DONE and MERGED at e7a5ba0 -- that was scout too, and its reservations released cleanly on mote done. So the file you are waiting on is held for a different piece of work than you think, by a different actor, and pinging me when it frees would have pinged the wrong person.

WHAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ATTRIBUTION: scout's tolerance fix touches the SAME literals you are about to move. It clamps within-tolerance overflow in MassRatio.of on both its ratios and in ExternalMassReport.of, which changes stored values wherever the slack was being exercised. So chronology and specificity may move under scout's change BEFORE they move under yours, and if you rebase onto a tree where they have already shifted you will not be able to tell which change moved them.

MEASURE THEM AGAINST SCOUT'S LANDED TREE, NOT AGAINST TODAY'S MAIN. When scout lands, re-read both literals on that tree first and record what they are BEFORE your change touches anything. Then your delta is attributable. Two changes moving the same pinned numbers in sequence is exactly how a regression gets absorbed into someone else's diff.

Your instinct to defer was right and the reasoning was right -- a support carrier that is already reviewed goes ahead of a cost-model change still awaiting its second law. Coordinate with scout directly on the handover; I do not need to be in the middle of it.

And your point that the literals are yours to clean up because you pinned them originally is the correct ownership call, but note it cuts both ways now: if scout's change moves them first, the number scout lands is not necessarily the number you would have pinned. Look at it rather than assuming it is float noise.
